name: Motor Prediction Error — How Architectural Surfaces and Spatial Demands Engage the Body's Forward Models
structural_pattern: The motor system generates forward models for every action (walking, climbing, reaching). Architecture that matches these predictions (optimal step heights, friction, door weights) produces motor fluency (low PE). Architecture that violates them produces motor prediction error (high PE), forcing movement from unconscious to conscious control. CALIBRATION (TP-II): Motor Fluency Index (MFI) = alpha_local / alpha_baseline. MFI < 1.0 indicates PE.
higher_order_principle: The body-as-prediction-system. Physical grace is the result of continuous low-PE motor prediction confirmation. Physical awkwardness is the result of continuous high-PE motor conflict. AGE MODERATION: Older adults face 1.5-4x attentional cost for the same MFI decrement.
transferable_to: Accessibility Design (predictable surfaces for impaired mobility)

causal_links.notes: Warren (1984) affordance thresholds. Deviation from optimal 0.25 x leg_length increases energy cost and control demand.
Tilted walls/floors challenge the postural synergy system (Latash, 2008).
High PE breaks flow, forcing attention to the body.

scope_conditions: Thresholds are body-scaled (dependent on user height/mobility)
moderators: User mobility status (Age factor: 20-40y=1.0x cost, 65-80y=1.5-2.5x cost, 80y+=2.5-4.0x cost)
Visual attention (distraction increases risk of PE)

interactions.nature: T8 describes the perception of affordances. TP1 describes the dynamic prediction error during the Execution of the afforded action.
TP1 provides the 'beat-to-beat' motor texture of the promenade.
Chronic motor PE feeds into interoceptive discomfort.

ecological_paradigm.design: Gait analysis on varied architectural surfaces
ecological_paradigm.protocol: Participants walk on stairs of varying riser heights and irregularity.
predictions: Deviation from optimum increases metabolic cost

key_references: Wolpert, D. M., et al. (1995). An internal model for sensorimotor integration.

### Template SOC1: Proxemic PE — Architecture as Mediator of Interpersonal Distance

```yaml
template_id: "PROXEMIC_PE_ARCH_001"
display_id: "SOC1"
name: "Proxemic Prediction Error — How Architecture Mediates Interpersonal Distance and the PE Consequences of Mismatch"

structural_pattern: >
  The brain generates a prediction of appropriate interpersonal
  distance based on relationship type, interaction purpose, and
  cultural norms — Hall's (1966) four-zone model: intimate
  (0–45cm), personal (45–120cm), social (1.2–3.6m), public
  (>3.6m). Architecture determines which zones are available,
  comfortable, and forced. Proxemic PE arises when actual
  interpersonal distance (as mediated by architecture) deviates
  from predicted appropriate distance.
  
  TWO DIRECTIONS OF PROXEMIC PE:
  
  TOO-CLOSE PE: Architecture forces closer proximity than the
  relationship warrants. Examples: elevator (intimate zone with
  strangers), narrow corridor (personal zone with strangers),
  open-plan office (sustained social-zone exposure to
  semi-strangers). Activates behavioral inhibition system
  (Keltner): gaze aversion, body stiffening, reduced
  movement, psychological withdrawal. Sustained too-close PE
  produces chronic social stress (Evans, T5/T29 pathway).
  
  TOO-FAR PE: Architecture enforces greater distance than the
  interaction requires. Examples: oversized meeting room
  (social zone for what should be personal-zone collaboration),
  hospital room with visitor chair far from bed (social zone
  for intimate-zone comfort), amphitheater classroom (public
  zone for what should be social-zone discussion). Produces
  approach-frustration PE: the social system predicts closer
  interaction and the architecture prevents it. Communication
  quality degrades (loss of facial microexpression reading,
  reduced vocal intimacy, impaired turn-taking).
  
  FURNITURE-SCALE MEDIATION (Sommer): Within any room, furniture
  arrangement provides the fine-grained proxemic control. Chair
  orientation (face-to-face vs. side-by-side vs. angle),
  table distance, partition height, and furniture fixity
  determine the proxemic regime. Sociofugal arrangements
  (parallel, distant, fixed) suppress interaction. Sociopetal
  arrangements (facing, close, moveable) facilitate interaction.
  The designer controls the proxemic prediction landscape at
  both the room scale and the furniture scale.

higher_order_principle: >
  Architecture is the primary mediator of interpersonal distance
  in built environments. The quality of social interaction
  depends on whether architectural and furniture design provides
  the proxemic zone appropriate for the intended interaction
  type. Proxemic PE is continuous, bidirectional, and
  architecturally controllable.
